active.title: Public Skate at Jay Lively Activity Center
active.description: Flagstaff's city ice rink runs cheap public-skate sessions year-round — wobble through your first laps or chase hockey-stop spray while the pines freeze outside.
active.bonus: Learn to skate backwards for one full lap — falling counts as trying.

active.title: Disc Golf at Fox Glenn Park
active.description: Fox Glenn's wooded course threads tight ponderosa corridors at 7,000 feet — precision throws, thin air, and a free round you'll feel in your lungs.
active.bonus: Play the entire round with only one disc — driver, midrange, putter, pick one and commit.

active.title: Climbing at Flagstaff Climbing
active.description: Flagstaff's dedicated indoor climbing gym lets you push grades on real movement-focused setting in a community that actually climbs outside.
active.bonus: Attempt a route two grades above your comfortable level and don't come off the wall without reaching the top hold.

active.title: Kachina Trail Traverse
active.description: This high-altitude contour trail through old-growth spruce and aspen delivers sweeping San Francisco Peaks views without the summit grind.
active.bonus: Find a clearing with a full southern panorama and identify at least two landmarks on the horizon.

active.title: Inner Basin Trail
active.description: A climb into the collapsed caldera at the heart of the San Francisco Peaks through groves of aspen — peak foliage country in late September.
active.bonus: Reach the Inner Basin and stand in the middle of the aspen grove in silence.

active.title: Picture Canyon Preserve
active.description: A natural and cultural preserve on the northeast edge of town with petroglyphs, a small waterfall and trails along the Rio de Flag.
active.bonus: Find at least three petroglyph panels along the canyon rim.

active.title: Schultz Creek Trail Mountain Bike
active.description: The fast, flowy singletrack descent through aspen and pine off Schultz Pass — the ride that made Flagstaff a mountain-bike town.
active.bonus: Ride the full descent cleanly without putting a foot down.

active.title: Fatman's Loop Trail
active.description: A rocky two-mile loop on the lower flank of Mount Elden, squeezing between giant boulders — short, scenic, and a real Flagstaff classic.
active.bonus: Find the namesake squeeze between the boulders and fit through it.

active.title: Lower Lake Mary Kayak
active.description: A shallow grassland reservoir southeast of town ringed by pines — flat-water paddling, birdlife, and Peaks views from the seat of a kayak.
active.bonus: Paddle to the far shore and drift back without dipping a paddle for a full minute.

active.title: Flagstaff Urban Trail System Ride
active.description: The 50-plus-mile network of paved and unpaved paths linking the whole town — rent or bring a bike and connect downtown to the pines car-free.
active.bonus: Ride from downtown to a trailhead entirely on the FUTS without touching a road.

active.title: Mount Elden Lookout Trail
active.description: A steep, switchbacking climb up the face of Mount Elden to the fire lookout at 9,300 feet — relentless up, enormous reward at the top.
active.bonus: Make the lookout without stopping more than three times on the way up.

active.title: Buffalo Park Loop
active.description: A two-mile crushed-cinder loop across an open meadow on McMillan Mesa with a full-frame view of the San Francisco Peaks — the local morning ritual.
active.bonus: Run or walk the full loop and watch the Peaks the entire way around.

social.title: Rack 'Em at Uptown Pubhouse
social.description: Flagstaff's downtown billiards hall pairs full-size tables with a serious whiskey list and zero sports-bar noise — chalk up, order a round, and settle in for the evening.
social.bonus: Play a stranger for the table — winner buys the round.

social.title: First Friday ArtWalk Downtown
social.description: On the first Friday of every month, downtown Flagstaff's galleries, shops, and bars open late with live music on the corners and the whole town drifting between Heritage Square and the Southside.
social.bonus: Buy something from every section of the market — produce, prepared food, and craft — spending under $20 total.

social.title: Live Show at Orpheum Theater
social.description: Flagstaff's 1917 downtown theater hosts touring acts and local legends in a room with real history soaked into every wall.
social.bonus: Get as close to the stage as possible and make eye contact with a performer at least once.

social.title: Open Mic at Firecreek Coffee
social.description: Firecreek's long-running open mic nights pull in a mix of NAU students, working musicians, and total surprises in a genuinely warm room.
social.bonus: Sign up and perform — one song, even if you haven't played in years.

social.title: State Bar
social.description: The downtown wine and craft-cocktail bar with a curated list and a calm, grown-up room — the antidote to the brewery circuit.
social.bonus: Let the bartender pour you a wine by the glass you would never have picked.

social.title: Monte Vista Cocktail Lounge
social.description: The basement bar beneath the historic (and famously haunted) 1927 Hotel Monte Vista downtown — dim, vintage, and full of stories.
social.bonus: Have a drink and ask the bartender which room is supposed to be haunted.

social.title: The Museum Club
social.description: The 1931 log-cabin roadhouse on Route 66 known as 'The Zoo' — a honky-tonk dance hall with a tree-trunk doorway and real country music history.
social.bonus: Two-step at least once, even badly, before the night is over.

social.title: Hops on Birch
social.description: The downtown beer bar on Birch Avenue with a wall of taps and a back patio — the reliable center of a Flagstaff night out.
social.bonus: Try a tap from an Arizona brewery you have never heard of.

social.title: Lumberyard Brewing Company
social.description: A big, family-friendly brewpub in a converted lumber building by the tracks — house beers, bar games, and room for a crowd.
social.bonus: Grab a seat by the windows and watch a freight train roll past mid-pint.

social.title: Dark Sky Brewing Company
social.description: The experimental brewery named for Flagstaff's dark-sky status, rotating dozens of small-batch beers you'll never find twice.
social.bonus: Order the strangest beer on the board and commit to a full pour.

social.title: Beaver Street Brewery
social.description: The long-running brewpub just south of the tracks — wood-fired pizza, house beer, and a beer garden that has anchored Southside for decades.
social.bonus: Split a brewhouse pizza and a sampler flight with whoever you came with.

social.title: Mother Road Brewing Company
social.description: Flagstaff's flagship brewery named for Route 66, with a Southside taproom and patio that draws the whole town for a pint after the trails.
social.bonus: Order the Tower Station IPA and find someone who just came off a peak hike.

foodie.title: Sandwiches at Proper Meats + Provisions
foodie.description: Flagstaff's Southside whole-animal butcher shop stacks its counter sandwiches — porchetta, pastrami, banh mi — with meat cut a few feet from where you're standing.
foodie.bonus: Ask the butcher what they'd take home tonight — buy whatever they say.

foodie.title: Dinner at Tinderbox Kitchen
foodie.description: Tinderbox turns local and regional ingredients into shareable small plates that make you realize Flagstaff's dining scene punches well above its size.
foodie.bonus: Let the server choose your entire meal — tell them your only restriction and hand it over completely.

foodie.title: Salsa Brava
foodie.description: The Flagstaff Mexican standby famous for its fresh roasted-salsa bar and Sonoran-style green chile — bright, fast, and beloved by locals.
foodie.bonus: Hit the salsa bar first and rank every salsa before your food arrives.

foodie.title: Josephine's Modern American Bistro
foodie.description: Fine dining inside a 1911 Craftsman bungalow near downtown — a patio under the trees and a menu that quietly outclasses the whole town.
foodie.bonus: Ask for the patio and order whatever the seasonal special is that night.

foodie.title: Karma Sushi
foodie.description: Downtown Flagstaff's go-to sushi bar on Aspen Avenue — surprisingly good fish for a high-desert mountain town, with a lively bar scene.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the sushi bar and let the chef send out one off-menu piece.

foodie.title: Criollo Latin Kitchen
foodie.description: The downtown Latin kitchen on San Francisco Street built around local and seasonal ingredients, with a killer happy hour and craft cocktails.
foodie.bonus: Build a meal entirely from the small plates and skip the entrées.

foodie.title: Diablo Burger
foodie.description: Heritage Square's local-beef burger joint serving open-range Arizona beef on a branded English muffin bun, with herb fries on the side.
foodie.bonus: Get the herb fries and a burger named off the chalkboard, not the regular menu.

foodie.title: Brandy's Restaurant & Bakery
foodie.description: The east-side breakfast institution where the baked goods come from the in-house bakery — eggs Benedict on a fresh croissant is the move.
foodie.bonus: Add a bakery item to your order even though the breakfast is already huge.

foodie.title: Macy's European Coffeehouse
foodie.description: The vegetarian coffeehouse that has roasted its own beans and fed Flagstaff's students and climbers since 1980 — the steamers are legendary.
foodie.bonus: Order a steamer and stay long enough to overhear at least one trailhead debate.

foodie.title: Tourist Home All Day Café
foodie.description: A restored 1920s boarding house for Basque sheepherders, now a bright Southside café with house pastries and a serious breakfast.
foodie.bonus: Get a pastry from the case before you even look at the menu.

foodie.title: MartAnne's Burrito Palace
foodie.description: The wildly colorful downtown spot famous for chilaquiles and mole — the line out front on weekend mornings is a Flagstaff institution.
foodie.bonus: Order the chilaquiles and finish the whole plate before the green chile defeats you.

foodie.title: Pizzicletta
foodie.description: The tiny Southside pizzeria turning out blistered Neapolitan pies from a wood oven, with house gelato to finish — a national-caliber pizza in a mountain town.
foodie.bonus: Order the margherita and a scoop of gelato, and eat at the counter watching the oven.

adventure.title: Trail Ride at Hitchin' Post Stables
adventure.description: This old-school outfit on Lake Mary Road has been putting riders on horseback through the pines and canyon country southeast of town for generations — no theatrics, just a real Western ride.
adventure.bonus: Ask for the most stubborn horse in the string and make friends with it by the end.

adventure.title: Sycamore Falls at Paradise Forks
adventure.description: This basalt gorge south of Williams pours snowmelt waterfalls in spring and draws Arizona's trad climbers year-round — walk the rim, watch the ropes go up, and peer into one of the state's least-known canyons.
adventure.bonus: Ask a climber what route they're on and watch them top out before you leave.

adventure.title: Red Mountain Trail
adventure.description: Twenty-five minutes northwest of town, a short cinder trail walks you straight into the eroded amphitheater of a million-year-old volcano — hoodoos, black cinder, and geology that feels illegal to touch.
adventure.bonus: Scramble into the amphitheater's back bowl and find a hoodoo taller than you — stand next to it for scale.

adventure.title: Elden Pueblo Archaeological Site
adventure.description: Walk directly among 800-year-old Sinaguan masonry walls at a site so rarely visited you'll likely have the ruins entirely to yourself.
adventure.bonus: Find the room outline that still has two full standing walls and sketch or photograph it from the corner angle.

adventure.title: Meteor Crater
adventure.description: Stand at the rim of a 50,000-year-old asteroid impact site — the best-preserved impact crater on Earth — and try to comprehend the scale.
adventure.bonus: Spot the six-foot astronaut training marker on the crater floor with your naked eye — no binoculars allowed.

adventure.title: Arizona Nordic Village Snowshoe
adventure.description: Strap on snowshoes and wander groomed trails through a silent ponderosa forest at 8,000 feet when the rest of town is inside.
adventure.bonus: Veer off on an ungroomed route for at least 10 minutes and navigate back without retracing your steps.

adventure.title: Lava River Cave
adventure.description: A mile-long lava tube northwest of town, pitch black and cold year-round — bring real lights and walk into the earth where lava once flowed.
adventure.bonus: Turn off every light for thirty seconds in the deepest part of the tube.

adventure.title: Arizona Snowbowl
adventure.description: The ski resort on the San Francisco Peaks — powder runs in winter, and a scenic chairlift to 11,500 feet for the views the rest of the year.
adventure.bonus: Ride the lift to the top and identify three landmarks from the summit deck.

adventure.title: Walnut Canyon National Monument
adventure.description: Cliff dwellings tucked into a sheer limestone canyon just east of town — the Island Trail drops you right past 700-year-old rooms.
adventure.bonus: Take the Island Trail and step into one of the cliff dwellings yourself.

adventure.title: Sunset Crater & Wupatki Loop
adventure.description: The 35-mile loop linking a young black cinder-cone volcano to ancestral Puebloan pueblos in red rock — two national monuments in one drive.
adventure.bonus: Walk the Lava Flow Trail at Sunset Crater, then stand inside the Wupatki ballcourt.

adventure.title: Grand Canyon South Rim Day Trip
adventure.description: The South Rim is only about 90 minutes north — drive up for a rim walk, a stretch down the Bright Angel Trail, and sunset over the canyon.
adventure.bonus: Hike at least fifteen minutes below the rim and back before you call it a day.

adventure.title: Humphreys Peak Summit
adventure.description: Arizona's highest point at 12,633 feet — a demanding climb through the San Francisco Peaks to a tundra summit with a hundred-mile view.
adventure.bonus: Reach the summit and find the Grand Canyon rim on the northern horizon.

chill.title: Sunset at Fort Tuthill County Park
chill.description: Wander the ponderosa loops of this southern-edge county park as the evening light goes gold between the pines — trails, open air, and almost nobody around on a weeknight.
chill.bonus: Stay until full dark and count five stars before you walk back to your car.

chill.title: Thorpe Park Hammock Session
chill.description: String a hammock between the pines at this sprawling neighborhood park and let the 7,000-foot elevation air and bird noise do the rest.
chill.bonus: Stay in the hammock for a minimum of 45 uninterrupted minutes with your phone face-down.

chill.title: Afternoon at Wheeler Park
chill.description: Flagstaff's oldest public park sits in the heart of downtown and offers a rare slow pocket of green surrounded by historic architecture.
chill.bonus: Strike up a real conversation with a stranger on a bench and learn one thing about Flagstaff you didn't know.

chill.title: Read at Bright Side Bookshop
chill.description: Flagstaff's beloved independent bookshop stocks an expertly curated selection and has just enough nook space to disappear into a book for an hour.
chill.bonus: Buy a book chosen entirely by the staff recommendation shelf — no reading the back cover first.

chill.title: Coconino Center for the Arts
chill.description: The community arts center near the Pioneer Museum showing regional artists and hosting the kind of exhibits that capture northern Arizona's character.
chill.bonus: See whatever is currently hanging and pick the one piece you would take home.

chill.title: Bookmans Flagstaff
chill.description: The beloved used-everything emporium on Milton Road — books, vinyl, instruments and oddities, and an easy hour to lose on a cold afternoon.
chill.bonus: Leave with one thing you did not know existed when you walked in.

chill.title: Pioneer Museum
chill.description: The Arizona Historical Society museum in an old stone hospital building on Fort Valley Road — logging, railroad and homestead history of the high country.
chill.bonus: Find the old steam locomotive parked outside and climb up to the cab.

chill.title: Historic Downtown & Heritage Square
chill.description: The walkable old railroad downtown around Heritage Square — brick storefronts, the train depot, buskers in summer, and the heart of Flagstaff.
chill.bonus: Watch a train roll through from Heritage Square and count the cars out loud.

chill.title: The Arboretum at Flagstaff
chill.description: A 200-acre high-elevation botanical garden in the ponderosa pines southwest of town, with native gardens and a birds-of-prey program.
chill.bonus: Catch the live raptor presentation and learn which hawks you saw on the trail.

chill.title: Museum of Northern Arizona
chill.description: The Fort Valley museum on the way to the Peaks covering the Colorado Plateau's geology, native cultures and art — the best primer on this whole region.
chill.bonus: Find the exhibit on the San Francisco Peaks before you go hike them.

chill.title: Riordan Mansion State Historic Park
chill.description: A sprawling 1904 Arts and Crafts log mansion built for two lumber-baron brothers — original furnishings and a guided walk through Flagstaff's gilded age.
chill.bonus: Take the guided tour and spot the Stickley furniture before the guide points it out.

chill.title: Lowell Observatory
chill.description: The 1894 hilltop observatory where Pluto was discovered — tour the historic Clark Telescope and look through the scopes after dark in true dark sky.
chill.bonus: Look through the historic Clark Telescope and find one object with your own eyes.
